blocks.text: 1. Context Deduplication

blocks.alt: Retrieved chunks have duplicates removed to produce unique context

blocks.text: Context Deduplication removes repeated information before the context gets assembled, catching a different kind of repetition from the one handled during ingestion.
It detects and removes chunks that repeat information already present elsewhere in the context, acting as a final redundancy check before the prompt is built.
2. Where Deduplication Reappears Here
Deduplication was already covered during ingestion, before chunks even reached the vector store.
Context deduplication catches a different, later kind of repetition, right before the final prompt is assembled.

blocks.text: 3. How Duplicates Still Slip Through

blocks.alt: Multiple retrievers and sources produce overlapping results

blocks.text: As in Multi-Query Retrieval, where each variation is searched separately, multiple query variations or ensemble members can retrieve overlapping content.
Even after ingestion time deduplication, repeated or highly similar chunks can still end up in the same final result set.
4. Exact Duplicates Versus Near Duplicates

blocks.alt: An exact duplicate is compared against a near-duplicate

blocks.text: The same exact versus near duplicate distinction from Deduplication reapplies at this later stage.
Exact repeats are easy to catch, but near duplicate paraphrases require a similarity check instead.
5. Why Repeated Content Wastes Budget

blocks.alt: A duplicate chunk wastes token budget

blocks.text: As covered in Token Budgeting, every part of the prompt takes space, and each repeated chunk consumes token budget without adding new information.
That wasted space could have held a different, useful chunk instead.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Two chunks that say almost the same thing in slightly different words still consume separate token budget, while providing the model with no additional information beyond what the first one already offered.

blocks.text: 6. Overlapping Parents From Parent Document Retrieval

blocks.alt: Child 1 and child 2 share the same parent

blocks.text: As covered in Parent Document Retrieval, deduping repeated parents there does not fully eliminate the problem: it can reappear here if it was not fully caught earlier.
Context deduplication acts as a final safety net for this kind of repetition.
7. Partial Overlap Is Harder Than Exact Match

blocks.alt: Partially overlapping text is harder to detect

blocks.text: Two chunks can share only part of their content rather than being fully identical.
Detecting that partial overlap requires more nuance than a simple exact match check.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A long parent chunk and a shorter chunk that repeats just its opening paragraph are not identical strings, yet still represent meaningful redundancy that a naive exact match check would miss.

blocks.text: 8. Deduplication Before Ordering And Compression
As covered in Context Ordering, deduplication interacts with context compression and filtering, fitting into the same pipeline sequence.
Removing redundant chunks before ordering and final assembly avoids wasted downstream work.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Context Deduplication Deserves A Dedicated Pass

blocks.alt: Multiple retrieval sources combined points toward using context deduplication

blocks.text: Pipelines using ensembles or multiple query variations need context deduplication.
Single method retrieval with tight upstream deduplication, by contrast, may rarely need this extra pass.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming ingestion time deduplication already caught every possible repeat at the context stage.
Checking only for exact text matches, missing paraphrased near duplicate content.
Running deduplication after ordering and compression instead of before them.
Skipping context deduplication for pipelines that use ensembles or multiple query variations.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Context deduplication removes chunks that repeat information already present elsewhere in the context.
It catches a later kind of repetition than ingestion time deduplication, right before the final prompt.
Multiple query variations or ensemble members can retrieve overlapping content even after earlier dedup.
Exact duplicates are easy to catch; near duplicate paraphrases need a similarity check.
Each repeated chunk consumes token budget without adding new information.
Overlapping parent chunks from parent document retrieval can reappear here as a related problem.
Detecting partial overlap between chunks requires more nuance than a simple exact match check.
Deduplication fits into the pipeline before ordering and final assembly.
